title: An artery throbs as it expands and recoils with each heartbeat
summary: OpenStax says a felt throb is an artery expanding and then recoiling, and that this movement reflects the heartbeat.
body: OpenStax says the throb is the expansion and recoiling of an artery, and that it reflects the heartbeat. The same section says blood pressure is the force blood exerts on vessel walls, with a systolic part from ventricular contraction and a diastolic part from relaxation. This card is that throb a person can feel in an artery. It does not give a normal rate, and it does not cover an uneven rhythm.

sources.title: 20.2 Blood Flow, Blood Pressure, and Resistance, chapter review
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology, first edition, web view, CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase of the pulse sentence: expansion and recoiling of an artery reflects the heartbeat. Systolic and diastolic are context, not the claim.
